note: THE 2026-08-26 (ROUND 8) RE-SHOOT, EXECUTABLE.
Round 7 shot every cell BEFORE two changes this branch then took: the settled
row on the setup rail (a decided gate row reads as the resolved-gate history
row) and the merge of main 803fe94045fe (cinatra#3006 — the schedule form stays
in the rail's schedule step after Continue, armed; no Trigger tab and no
'Trigger configuration' card anywhere; the breadcrumb and the tab say
'Schedule'). A picture taken before a change is the record of what came before
it, so ALL SEVEN cells are taken again here on the fixed head — C7, C9, C10,
C10b, C10c, C11, C11b, light and dark. The set's other sixteen pictures are
byte-identical and the canonical capture index is untouched.
The runs are the app's own, asked for in the app's own chat with a real model
provider and created by the app's own dispatch. Nothing here inserts a run, a
trigger, a park, a gate or a record; every number is read back from the rows.
SIX RUNS, because one run cannot hold every reading at once. The reasons are
properties of the screen, and one of them CHANGED with cinatra#3006:
- a one-off armed ahead no longer leaves the setup surface — the form stays
in the schedule step — but arming it still moves the run out of the
first-shown state C7 needs, so C7/C10b stand on one run that was never
pressed and C9 on a second that was;
- the recommendation hold only fires for an agent that HAS a candidate skill,
and a hold can be live OR decided but not both, so C10 (live) and C10c
(decided) stand on two runs of the agent that has one, assigned through the
app's own Matches tab;
- the review step needs a run that produced a reviewable artifact, and its
*working* reading lives only in the window between the artifact's pending
outbox row and the gate the sweeper opens from it — measured at 28.8 s and
27.2 s on this lane — so C11b's two themes come from two runs, and C11 is
shot on the first of them once its gate is on file.

cells.name: run-setup-scheduling-step
cells.requires: the run-surface drawing's two-column clause — 'a step rail down the left NAMES the run's ordered steps, and the run detail on the right shows the selected step' — on the first-time run page, with the unchanged scheduling form ('When should this run?', the option rows, Estimated run duration, Continue) open in the RIGHT column and no agentic run progress card beside it (plan (A) 7.2 step 5); the breadcrumb and the tab say 'Schedule', never 'Trigger' (cinatra#3006). cinatra#2970 acceptance 1 and 4.

cells.name: run-setup-continue-armed
cells.requires: cinatra#2970 acceptance 2, second half — 'Continue arms it exactly as today' — read with today's main (cinatra#3006): the SAME run page after Continue was pressed on the scheduler step, with the one-off armed AHEAD and the armed form STILL INSIDE the schedule step; no Trigger tab and no 'Trigger configuration' card anywhere; the breadcrumb and the tab say 'Schedule'.

cells.name: run-setup-recommendation-step-opened
cells.proofNote: the recommendation row pressed on a run with a LIVE hold
cells.requires: cinatra#2970 acceptance 3, first half — 'the skills-recommendation step ... opens the same way, to the right of the steps, never under a row' — and the fix on this head: 'the recommendation row opens exactly when the run has a live hold (the hold card)'.

cells.name: run-setup-recommendation-row-closed
cells.proofNote: a FORCED press on the closed recommendation row of a run with no park
cells.requires: the fix's other half — 'closed+muted otherwise' — and the ruling's 'clicking it does nothing; the scheduler stays open; the right column never shows an empty step surface'. The press is FORCED because the row carries aria-disabled and Playwright's own actionability treats that as not-enabled: a row that is never pressed proves nothing.

cells.name: run-setup-recommendation-step-settled
cells.proofNote: the settled recommendation row pressed after the hold was decided on the card
cells.requires: the fix: 'the recommendation row opens exactly when the run has a live hold (the hold card) or a DECIDED one (the settled row)' — the settled chip in the detail column; AND the ratified drawing's resolved-gate history reading, 'A resolved gate stays on the rail as read-only history — its entry keeps its place and records how it was settled': the completed circle (the check glyph) in place of the numeral and the title unhighlighted.

cells.name: run-setup-review-step-opened
